title: Import holding-time rules
purpose: Create or change holding-time rules from one CSV file: check every row in a preview, then save all rows or none.
summary: Create or change holding-time rules from one CSV file. You check every row in a preview first, then all rows are saved or none. Only admins can import holding-time rules.

tasks.title: Import a file of holding-time rules
steps: Download [[holding-rules-template.csv]] and add one row per record below the header. Open [[Columns]] to see what each column needs.
Save the sheet as CSV (UTF-8), choose it in [[CSV file (UTF-8)]], and select [[Check file]].
Read the preview. When it says Ready, select the Import button, which names the number of rows.

tasks.title: Change existing holding-time rules
steps: Identify each rule by its method version, matrix, start event and end event.
Leave out the columns you don't want to change. A blank cell clears an optional value.
Check the file, fill in [[Reason for changing existing records]], and import it.

tasks.title: Fix a file with errors
steps: Read the Errors column. Each error names its line and column, and rows with errors are listed first.
Correct the file, select [[Upload a corrected file]], and check it again. Nothing was saved.

good_to_know: Nothing is saved until you import the checked preview, and any error blocks the whole file.
A row finds its rule by method version, matrix, analyte, start event and end event. A blank analyte means the rule for the whole method.
An import never creates records of another type. The method versions the rules name must exist first.
Durations are in hours, as on the manual form (48 is 2 days). A calendar period such as 6 months needs the hours the laboratory has decided on.
The uploaded file is not kept. History records its file name and SHA-256 digest, so keep your copy.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Holding-time rules can be imported by administrators only, the same roles that may create and change them by hand. Every row is saved through the same service as manual entry, which checks the role again. Other staff and client portal accounts are refused this page, its template and its import, whatever links they see.

items.label: CSV file (UTF-8)
items.description: Required. Save the sheet as CSV (UTF-8): comma separated, standard quoting, a leading byte-order mark allowed. The first line is the header; no title rows above it. Up to 1024 KiB and 2000 nonblank data rows; blank lines are ignored. Excel workbooks are not read, because a workbook hands numbers over as binary floating-point values and limits must stay exact decimals.

items.label: Header
items.description: Column names are matched after trimming spaces and ignoring case. An unknown, unnamed or duplicate column, or a missing key column, blocks the whole file with a message naming it. Data columns may be left out; see How rows match records.

items.label: holding-rules-template.csv
items.description: Downloads a file holding only the header row, with a byte-order mark so spreadsheet programs read it as UTF-8. Add one row per record below it.

items.label: Check file
items.description: Reads the file and shows the preview. Nothing is saved.

items.label: Cancel
items.description: Returns to Spreadsheet import without importing.

sections.title: Columns
paragraphs: The Columns section under the file field (collapsed; open it to see the table) lists the same information. Text is stripped of surrounding spaces and otherwise kept exactly. Values are not converted: numbers are plain decimals (digits 0-9 with an optional point and sign; no exponent, thousands separator, unit or symbol, and no more digits than the field holds), choices are the listed codes exactly as written, and yes/no columns accept yes, no, true or false. A value that does not fit is an error naming its line and column, never a guess.

items.label: method_code
items.description: Key, required. Text. Code of an existing method version, for example EPA 200.8.

items.label: method_version
items.description: Key, required. Text. Version of that method, as recorded.

items.label: matrix
items.description: Key, required. One of: water, wastewater, soil. Matrix of the test.

items.label: analyte
items.description: Key, optional. Text. Name of an existing analyte with a test of this method and matrix (or a test this method prepares), to limit the rule to it. Blank or left out: the rule applies to every analyte of the method. An analyte's rule replaces the method-wide rule with the same start and end events for that analyte.

items.label: start_event
items.description: Key, required. One of: collection, preparation. Event that starts the clock.

items.label: end_event
items.description: Key, required. One of: preparation, analysis. Event that stops the clock.

items.label: name
items.description: Required for a new record; cannot be blank. Text, up to 120 characters. Rule name shown on the holding-time clock.

items.label: duration_hours
items.description: Required for a new record; cannot be blank. Hours as a decimal number (digits 0-9), at most 2 decimal places, at least 0.01. Maximum time from the start event to the end event, in hours (28 days = 672).

items.label: warning_hours
items.description: Optional; blank clears it. Hours as a decimal number (digits 0-9), at most 2 decimal places, at least 0.01. Flag as at risk when this much time or less remains. Blank means no warning.

items.label: basis
items.description: Optional; blank clears it. Text. Method or SOP reference for this rule.

items.label: active
items.description: Optional; cannot be blank. yes or no. Whether the record is available for new work. A new record is active unless this says no.

sections.title: How rows match records
paragraphs: A row matches the holding-time rule of the same method version, matrix, analyte, start event and end event. A blank analyte, or a file without the analyte column, matches the method-wide rule and never an analyte's rule; analyte names are compared without regard to case. The method version must already exist, and so must the analyte and its test of this method and matrix (or a test this method prepares) when the row names one.

A row whose key matches an existing record changes it; a row whose key matches none creates a record. Records are found by these keys, never by database IDs. A column absent from the file leaves that value of existing records alone. A column present with a blank cell clears an optional value; it is an error for a required one. A new record needs every required column, and an omitted optional column takes the same default as a new record entered by hand (active unless active says no).

A row may refer only to records that already exist in the referenced type; a missing reference is an error naming it, and nothing is created in another record type. Two rows for the same record are an error.

Durations are entered in hours, as on the manual form: a decimal number with at most 2 decimal places and at least 0.01 (0.25 is 15 minutes, 48 is 2 days, 672 is 28 days). The value is converted to whole seconds. A calendar period such as 6 months has no fixed number of hours; enter the hours the laboratory has decided on. A clock that starts at preparation can only end at analysis.

sections.title: Preview
paragraphs: The preview runs every row through the same checks and services as saving, in a transaction that is then undone, so it shows exactly what Import would do and stores nothing. The undone attempt can use up record ID numbers, so IDs of later records may skip. Any error blocks the whole file.

The summary above the table says whether the file is ready or how many errors it has; file-level errors (header, encoding, size, malformed CSV) are listed there. The table heading counts the rows to create, to change, unchanged and with errors.

items.label: Line
items.description: Line in the file where the row starts. The header is line 1.

items.label: Action
items.description: Create, Change, Unchanged, or Error. An unchanged row is not saved and leaves no history.

items.label: Record
items.description: The key the row names, as it would be found or created.

items.label: Values (before → after)
items.description: For a change, every changed value with the current value struck through and the new one after it; blank means empty. For a new record, the values it receives. Values are shown exactly, without storage padding.

items.label: Errors
items.description: Every problem in the row, each naming its column. Rows with errors are listed first. Locked identity values, missing reasons and other rules are reported with the same message as manual editing. A row that fails for an unexpected reason is reported with its line, and nothing is imported.

items.label: Reason for changing existing records
items.description: Shown and required when the file changes at least one existing record. One reason applies to every changed row. Kept with your text if the import is refused.

items.label: Import … rows
items.description: Available when the preview has no errors. Reads the file again, refuses it if the file or any record it changes differs from the preview, then saves every row in one transaction or none. A refused import shows a new preview to check and import again.

items.label: Start over
items.description: Discards the preview and returns to an empty upload form.

items.label: Upload a corrected file
items.description: Shown when the preview has errors. Correct the file and check it again; nothing was saved.

items.label: Cancel
items.description: Returns to Spreadsheet import without importing.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Each created or changed record gets its usual history entry from its service. A created record's reason reads Created by import of the file name and the file's SHA-256 digest; a changed record's reason is your reason followed by the file name and digest. One further event records the file: record type, file name, SHA-256, size and the counts. The uploaded file itself is not kept; keep your copy, which the digest identifies. After a successful import the page opens the list where the records appear, with a message giving the counts.
